title: Ramayana Becomes First Indian Film to Release in ScreenX Format Worldwide
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic secures deal with CJ 4DPLEX for nearly 1,300 premium-format auditoriums ahead of its Diwali 2026 release
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 will release in ScreenX and 4DX formats through a deal with CJ 4DPLEX, marking the first time an Indian film has been presented in the 270-degree ScreenX format.
  • The agreement covers close to 1,300 ScreenX and 4DX auditoriums worldwide, with specific sequences formatted for the immersive side-wall and motion-seat experiences.
  • The film, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, and Sunny Deol, is set for a global release on November 6, 2026, with India following on November 8 for Diwali.
  • With an estimated budget of around $400–500 million for both parts, Ramayana is the most expensive Indian film ever made and has Sony handling global distribution.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 will become the first Indian film ever released in the ScreenX format, after its producers struck a deal with CJ 4DPLEX to place the epic across nearly 1,300 premium-format auditoriums worldwide, according to Variety India.

The agreement also covers 4DX screens, giving the film two distinct immersive presentation options when it opens during Diwali 2026 — internationally on November 6 and in India on November 8.

What ScreenX and 4DX Actually Look Like

ScreenX is a multi-projection system developed by South Korean company CJ 4DPLEX that extends selected portions of a film onto the left and right walls of an auditorium, creating a 270-degree field of view. Rather than projecting the entire runtime across three screens, filmmakers choose specific action and dramatic sequences for the wraparound treatment, pulling those moments into the audience's peripheral vision while the rest of the film plays on the standard front screen.

https://x.com/Filmyscoopss/status/2089273905974563065

For Ramayana, the production has formatted specific battle and dramatic beats for the side-wall presentation — sequences where the expanded visual field can enhance the scale of the epic's mythology-driven set pieces.

4DX takes a different approach. Instead of widening the image, it layers physical sensation onto the viewing experience through motion-enabled seating and environmental effects — movement, vibration, wind, water, snow, scent, and lighting cues timed to on-screen action. The Ramayana team has built sequences specifically for 4DX playback, according to the production.

The deal follows the success of Sony Pictures' Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which became the highest-grossing ScreenX release in India and was the first film shot specifically for the format.

A Record-Setting Production

Produced by Namit Malhotra under Prime Focus Studios alongside DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is a two-part live-action adaptation of Valmiki's ancient Sanskrit epic. The combined budget for both installments has been estimated at $400–500 million, making it the most expensive Indian film production in history — more than five times the reported budget of S.S. Rajamouli's RRR.

The cast is led by Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as the demon king Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, and Ravie Dubey — making his film debut — as Lakshmana. The ensemble also includes Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, and veteran actor Arun Govil, who played Rama in the iconic 1987 television series.

"In over 100 years of Hollywood and the Indian film industry, this will be the first film ever that hits mainstream theatrical release worldwide by a Hollywood studio and an Indian movie coming together."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer, Prime Focus Studios

The score comes from a collaboration between Oscar winners Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman — Zimmer's first full-fledged involvement with an Indian film production. Shridhar Raghavan wrote the screenplay, while Ravi Bansal and Ramsey Avery lead production design. Terry Notary and Guy Norris oversee action choreography.

Sony's Global Distribution Push

In a move announced at San Diego Comic-Con, Sony Pictures acquired global distribution rights for Ramayana — a first-of-its-kind arrangement between a Hollywood major and an Indian production of this scale. The film is set for release across an estimated 50,000 international screens, with an English-language version in which the principal cast members dub their own dialogue rather than relying on voice actors.

Global exhibitor John Fithian, who helped broker exhibition partnerships at CinemaCon 2026, has said major theatrical chains from the U.S., Canada, Latin America, Europe, and Australia attended private screenings. Fithian described the film as potentially "the first Indian global theatrical blockbuster ever."

Part Two Already in Production

Filming for Ramayana: Part 1 took place at Film City in Mumbai from April 2024 through July 2025. The second installment is currently in production and is scheduled for a Diwali 2027 worldwide release.

With the ScreenX and 4DX deal locked, the premium-format rollout adds to an already aggressive global distribution strategy. For the Indian film industry, the ScreenX first is another signal of how Ramayana's producers are positioning the project not as a regional event but as a mainstream global release competing directly with Hollywood tentpoles.
